newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-BULLETS NAME BICKERSTAFF HEAD COACH.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-BULLETS NAME BICKERSTAFF HEAD COACH.

text.p: Bernie Bickerstaff stepped down from the Denver Nuggets front office to take over as head coach of the Washington Bullets on Monday.

Bickerstaff resigned his position as president and general manager of the Nuggets to return to the team he served as an assistant coach for 12 years, including 1978 when the Bullets won their only NBA title.
"I am glad that he's back home, where he belongs," said Bullets general manager Wes Unseld at a news conference at the team's Bowie State University practice site.
"I am very familiar with his coaching, and he's a great addition to our organisation," added Unseld, who was the centre on that 1978 championship team.

"I think I'm very fortunate to come back here where I've been, with an organisation that gave me my start," said Bickerstaff, who was the club's top assistant under coach Dick Motta from 1973 to 1985.
The underachieving Bullets, mired in fourth place in the Atlanta Division with a 22-25 mark, fired coach Jim Lynam last Wednesday.
Bickerstaff, 52, was in his seventh year with the Nuggets' organisation, where he had served as the team's coach, executive vice president, president and general manager.
In his first full season as Nuggets coach last year, Bickerstaff posted a 35-47 record. He had a coaching record of 59-68 in parts of three seasons with Denver.
Bickerstaff also served as head coach of the Seattle SuperSonics for five years from 1985-86 to 1989-90, compiling a 202-208 record and three postseason appearances.
